title: webhook://
description:
`webhook://`: HTTP endpoints described by OpenAPI 3.1; every accepted request is an
item, shown as a row. Two endpoints run while the dashboard does: a **GET without a
token** (left, port 8765) and a **POST with a token** (right, port 8766). Press `K` on
a panel for the curl commands that send it data. See `:help dbdash-webhook`.

show.title: GET, no token (:8765)
show.description:
A **GET without a token**: no body, so the query parameters are the item, checked
and converted by the document (`n` must be a number, `tags` is a comma list,
missing ones take their defaults). It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so it may go
without a token. Send some:
```sh
curl "http://127.0.0.1:8765/hooks/ping?user=ann&n=3&tags=a,b"
curl "http://127.0.0.1:8765/hooks/ping"
```
The reply is the document's example, `{"pong": true}`. An invalid parameter is
refused with 400 and nothing is added:
```sh
curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8765/hooks/ping?n=many"
```

query.sql:
openapi: 3.1.0
info: { title: events, version: "1" }
# any one of these: a bearer token, an API key header, Basic user:password
security: [ { bearer: [] }, { apikey: [] }, { basic: [] } ]
paths:
  /events/{source}:
    post:
      operationId: events
      parameters:
        - { name: source, in: path, required: true, schema: { type: string, enum: [web, app] } }
        - { name: X-Request-Id, in: header, schema: { type: string } }
        - { name: region, in: cookie, schema: { type: string, default: "us" } }
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/x-ndjson:
            schema: { $ref: "openapi/events.schema.yaml#/Event" }
      responses: { "202": { description: queued } }
  /forms:
    post:
      operationId: forms
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/x-www-form-urlencoded: { schema: { $ref: "openapi/events.schema.yaml#/Event" } }
          multipart/form-data: { schema: { $ref: "openapi/events.schema.yaml#/Event" } }
      responses: { "202": { description: queued } }
  /logs:
    post:
      operationId: logs
      requestBody:
        content:
          text/x-log: { schema: { type: string, pattern: "^\\w+ \\w+$" } }
      responses: { "202": { description: queued } }
components:
  securitySchemes:
    bearer: { type: http, scheme: bearer }               # Authorization: Bearer <token>
    apikey: { type: apiKey, in: header, name: X-API-Key } # X-API-Key: <key>
    basic: { type: http, scheme: basic }                 # Authorization: Basic (curl -u)
query.transform:
-- rs: one item; params: { path, query, header, cookie }; request: method, path,
-- operation_id, content_type, headers (without credentials).
store.events = store.events or {}
local what
if request.operation_id == "logs" then
  what = rs
else
  what = ("%s %s%s"):format(rs.user, rs.action, rs.amount and (" " .. rs.amount) or "")
end
local from = params.path.source or request.operation_id
local region = params.cookie.region or ""
table.insert(store.events, 1, { os.date("%H:%M:%S"), from, region, what })
while #store.events > 10 do table.remove(store.events) end
return { columns = { "at", "from", "region", "event" }, rows = store.events }

show.title: POST, with a token (:8766)
show.description:
A **POST with a token**: every request needs a credential, any one of the three
ways the document's `security` lists (`database.options.tokens` holds the values):
```sh
# a bearer token (either of the two in the list)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" -d "user=cat&action=logout" \
     http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/forms
# an API key header
curl -H "X-API-Key: demo-key" -d "user=cat&action=logout" \
     http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/forms
# Basic user:password
curl -u demo:secret -d "user=cat&action=logout" http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/forms
# no credential, or a wrong one: 401 with WWW-Authenticate
curl -i -d "user=cat&action=logout" http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/forms
```
Keep a real token out of the file: `tokens: { bearer: "${EVENTS_TOKEN}" }` reads it
from the environment (start Neovim with `EVENTS_TOKEN=...`), and senders use
`-H "Authorization: Bearer $EVENTS_TOKEN"`. Tokens are compared in constant time
and never shown in `request`, errors or replies.

**Events**, one JSON object per line (`application/x-ndjson`), each checked
against the Event schema; the path picks the source (`web` or `app`):
```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
     -H "X-Request-Id: r1" --cookie "region=eu" \
     --data-binary $'{"user": "ann", "action": "login"}\n{"user": "bob", "action": "purchase", "amount": 9.5}\n' \
     http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/events/web
```

**A form** (urlencoded or multipart) is one item:
```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" \
     -F user=dan -F action=login http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/forms
```

**Log lines** (`text/x-log`): one item per line:
```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer demo-token" -H "Content-Type: text/x-log" \
     --data-binary $'eve login\nfay logout\n' http://127.0.0.1:8766/hooks/logs
```

A request the document does not allow gets `application/problem+json`: 401
without a valid credential, 400 for an invalid event (try `"action": 1`), 403 for
an `Origin` other than `http://localhost:3000`. See `:help dbdash-webhook-security`.
